binders: A Poisson parameter lambda and a random variable X with distribution Pois(lambda) (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 opening sentence).
A real deviation threshold t, universally quantified subject to t in (0,lambda] (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 second sentence).

A positive absolute real constant c, inherited from the immediately preceding small-deviation inequality and used in the displayed bound (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5 phrase 'c > 0 is an absolute constant' and Exercise 2.3.6 display).
hypotheses: X has Poisson distribution with parameter lambda (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 opening sentence).
The deviation threshold satisfies 0 < t <= lambda (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 second sentence).
conclusions: The probability of the inclusive two-sided event |X-lambda| >= t is at most 2 exp(-c t^2/lambda) (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 displayed inequality).
definitions_and_conventions: Pois(lambda) denotes the Poisson distribution with parameter lambda (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 opening sentence; PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.3).
The center lambda is the Poisson mean, as confirmed by Remark 2.3.7's description of the near-mean normal comparison N(lambda,lambda) (PDF page 9, printed page 20).

The constant c is absolute: it is a numerical positive constant independent of X, lambda, and t; no numerical value is specified (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5 immediately preceding Exercise 2.3.6).
implicit_context: Probability is taken under the ambient law of X (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 displayed probability).

The interval condition 0 < t <= lambda makes the claim a near-mean or small-deviation estimate and entails lambda > 0 whenever an admissible t is chosen (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 and Remark 2.3.7).
The hint treats the Poisson law as obtainable from Bernoulli sums through the Poisson limit theorem, Theorem 1.3.4 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6 hint).

details: X has the one-parameter Poisson law Pois(lambda), and lambda is the center in the deviation event (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6).
The event is two-sided and inclusive: |X-lambda| >= t (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
The threshold t is additive rather than relative, while its permitted range is capped by lambda (same exercise statement).
The exponent is quadratic in t and inversely proportional to lambda: -c t^2/lambda; the prefactor is exactly 2 (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
Remark 2.3.7 identifies this as the normal-like small-deviation regime for Pois(lambda) (PDF page 9, printed page 20).

The absolute constant c must be independent of the Poisson parameter and deviation threshold (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.5's immediately preceding absolute-constant convention and Exercise 2.3.6 formula).

The hint directs the reader to transfer Exercise 2.3.5 through the Poisson limit theorem, Theorem 1.3.4 (PDF page 9, printed page 20); this is proof guidance and does not add a hypothesis to the claim.

undebatable_constraints: X must have Poisson distribution Pois(lambda) (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6).
The threshold domain is exactly 0 < t <= lambda (PDF page 9, printed page 20, Exercise 2.3.6).
The deviation event is the inclusive two-sided event |X-lambda| >= t (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
The bound has prefactor 2 and exponential rate -c t^2/lambda (PDF page 9, printed page 20, displayed inequality).
The constant c is positive and absolute rather than dependent on lambda or t (PDF page 9, printed page 20, the convention established immediately in Exercise 2.3.5).

contract_plain_english: There is a universal numerical constant c > 0 such that if X has Poisson distribution with parameter lambda, then for every real threshold t with 0 < t <= lambda, the probability that X differs from its mean lambda by at least t is at most 2 exp(-c t^2/lambda). This is the source's two-sided, normal-like small-deviation bound near the Poisson mean; the hint derives it from the preceding Bernoulli small-deviation estimate by the Poisson limit theorem.
